title: Bunn's philosophy as a bandleader: equal shares and fines
summary: As a leader he split pay equally, fined latecomers into a trust fund, and contrasts Edgar Hayes wanting everything.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Well, some people -- being a leader is --
They take advantage. They really do take advantage of you.
They don't know how to handle it sometimes.
What was your philosophy when you were a leader, yourself?

Let everybody do their thing. That was my philosophy. And whenever we went into a job that was going to get paid, I was the leader, they had their money coming, I had it ready for them when they come off. And it kept down arguments, you know, disagreements.
According to the union now the leader's supposed to get double, but a lot of leaders take more than double.
Well, I didn't. I split it.
I'd take an equal share with them. Because what the hell's the use -- we're both up there doing the same thing.
Yeah. Well, that's the way I've always felt.
But a lot of people get on this power --
"When I'm the leader I get the most." That's bullshit. You get the most, you go on up there and do
Well, some leaders feel -- it depends. Like if a leader's also a manager, if he's getting the gigs -- like sometimes the group doesn't have an agent.
And the leader's also being the agent.
Well, then I would think maybe he deserves more.
No. We had the groups different.
We split whatever we got, we split with each other.
But Edgar wanted it all because his name was Edgar Hayes.
"I'm Edgar Hayes. Stardusters." In other words, we was just his help. We was helping each other. And that's the way we saw it. So Edgar saw it different, and that's why I knocked the shit out of him.
How did you feel about -- when you were a leader how did you feel about people flaking out on you? You know, showing up late for the gig and stuff like that.
Take it out of their money.

That's right. And when the night came, the job was finished and we were getting paid, I had to fine them. I said, 'This is a fine. We'll put this in the trust fund.' And that's the way it stayed. And we got along. But shit, Edgar Hayes, man, he wanted everything. That's why I knocked the shit out of him with that guitar. Showing off. Right in San Francisco. He didn't do that no more. Have you ever heard of Edgar Hayes?
